chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Waddad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

My father (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Four qualities, whoever possesses them, their faith is complete, and even if there were sins between his head and his feet, that would not diminish it.' He said: 'They are truthfulness, fulfilling trusts, modesty, and good character.'
ai.seo_question: What four qualities ensure the perfection of faith according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) from his father Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), highlights that truthfulness, fulfilling trusts, modesty, and good character are the pillars that preserve faith (iman) even amidst abundant sins. In Shia scholarship, these four traits are often viewed as the external manifestations of inner spiritual integrity, ensuring that one's deeds are accepted and their faith remains robust. The emphasis on 'husn al-khuluq' (good character) underscores the practical application of faith in daily interactions, a key theme in al-Tusi's Tahdhib al-Ahkam.
